label: observability-and-operability-of-new-path
name: New state, path, counter or option lands without a way to see it, measure it, or reach it through the launcher everyone uses
description: What breaks: an operator cannot inspect, measure or invoke the feature. New PosDevice fields (prev_cmd_kind, reuse counters) not added to the existing debug_string dump (3405051930 'add these to the debug_string utility?'); a new allocator with no TRACE_EVENTs and no 'memory' Perfetto category at all (3235915961, explicitly no action required); new Perfetto memory captures described in words with no screenshot (5271922621); page-share counters as a compile-time option printed at exit where FUSE with env-var opt-in would allow live and interval reads (5156698046 'I'm ok approving this as-is, although'); a new runtron option --trace-passes not accepted or forwarded by perfetto/tronperf, the wrapper every developer launches through (5106398334 part 2 'that script needs an update'; part 1 of the same id, the body calling a runtron flag a 'Perfetto option', is a claim-wider-than-code nit). Procedure: when a struct with a debug_string/dump/operator<< gains members, check the helper prints them; when a new subsystem lands with no TRACE_EVENT/TRON_CHECKPOINT, ask whether its cost can be measured; when the PR adds user-visible output, ask for a sample; when a counter is build-time and exit-printed, point to the existing runtime stats layer; for every new command-line option, env var or config knob grep bin/, perfetto/ and ci scripts for wrappers that forward sibling options. Mostly 'no action required' or 'ok approving as-is' questions.
disposition_reason: No existing check asks whether a new path is observable or wired into the launcher; 5 rows over 5 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes for the debug_string gap, the missing-trace scan and the wrapper grep; the FUSE alternative needs knowledge of the stats layer (grep attn_stats / set_value / README.stats.md).

members.concern: The new PosDevice state fields (prev_cmd_kind, prev_*_wcmd_index, reuse counters) should be included in the existing PosDevice::debug_string dump so they show in debug output.

detection.trigger: a diff adds data members to a struct or class that already has a debug_string(), dump(), operator<< or format helper, and the diff does not touch that helper
detection.procedure: for each struct in h/ gaining members, grep the same header for 'debug_string' or 'fmt::format' members on that type (device.hpp:493 declares PosDevice::debug_string(bool include_offsets, ...)); check whether the diff adds the new members to that helper's body
detection.question: Does the type's existing debug/print helper print the new members, and if not, would an operator reading a debug log be unable to see the new state?

members.quote: add these to the `debug_string` utility for printing?
members.note: No reply in the digest, but at the final head a62d15a3dc h/pos/device.hpp:599-600 prints legacy_wcmd_reuse_count, attn_wcmd_reuse_count and prev_legacy_wcmd_index inside debug_string (verified with git show), so the ask was applied. Comment was posted on commit a62d15a3dc per the digest header, which is the final head; the line numbers (403/405) match the member block there.

members.concern: Wade asks whether the allocator paths (drain_reserves() walk over all arenas, allocate, deallocate) should emit Perfetto TRACE_EVENTs so their cost can be measured, and notes there is no 'memory' Perfetto category at all; explicitly no action required.

detection.trigger: The PR adds a new subsystem or hot path (allocator, scheduler step, loop over all N items under a lock) with no TRACE_EVENT / TRON_CHECKPOINT / counter in any added line.
detection.procedure: grep the diff's added src/ lines for TRACE_EVENT|TRON_CHECKPOINT; grep h/common/perfetto.hpp for a category matching the subsystem name; if both absent, ask (as a non-blocking question) whether the walk/loop cost should be observable and whether a category is missing.
detection.question: Could an operator measure the cost of this new path in a trace today, and if not, is that a deliberate choice?

members.quote: wouldn't it be useful to have some TRACE_EVENTs we can gather metrics across these memory paths? Might be worth knowing the cost of walks like this, etc. I noticed we don't even currently have a "memory" category defined for Perfetto. That seems like a gap?
members.note: Wade read h/common/perfetto.hpp (or its category list) outside the diff to state no 'memory' category exists. He wrote 'No action needed, just inquiring.' Author confirmed the gap (10 categories, none for memory, no allocator emits TRACE_EVENT), flagged the ~20 ns/op hot-path cost as a reason to keep such a category off by default, and filed STORY-461. No code change in this PR.

members.concern: Wade asks the author to share screenshots of the new Perfetto memory captures so a reader can see what the feature produces.

detection.trigger: The PR adds user-visible instrumentation or output (trace events, a dashboard, a log format) and the body describes it in words only, with no image, trace excerpt or decoded sample.
detection.procedure: Read the PR body for any attached image, trace file or decoded event dump; if none, ask for one.
detection.question: Does the PR show what the new output looks like, or only describe it?

members.quote: Do you happen to have a couple screen shots of these new memory captures you could share?
members.note: Posted one minute after the second inline comment. The body claims 'DUT captures validated the expected memory events and annotations' but attaches nothing. Wade approved the next day regardless, so the ask was not a condition.

members.concern: Wade approves as-is but asks whether the author considered publishing the page-share counters through FUSE (the server's live statistics file interface) with env-var opt-in, so they could be read while the process runs and measured over chosen intervals instead of as a compile-time option printed at process exit.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a new counter, histogram or diagnostic that is enabled by a compile-time option (CMake option, #ifdef) and reported once (stderr print at exit, log line, destructor of a static), in a code base that already has a runtime statistics interface (grep h/ and src/ for the stats/FUSE publishing layer, e.g. `attn_stats`, `set_value`, README.stats.md).
detection.procedure: Find the existing live-publishing mechanism (README.stats.md; the FUSE layer that stores one value per file, see memory attn-stats-why-not-fuse.md) and its opt-in convention (env var at process start). Compare the PR's mechanism on three axes: build-time versus runtime enable, one-shot versus live readable, whole-run versus interval measurement. If the existing mechanism gives all three for the same counters, write the finding as a question with the two alternatives and state it is not a condition of approval.
detection.question: Could these counters be exposed through the repository's existing runtime statistics interface with runtime opt-in, giving live and interval reads, instead of a build option and an exit-time print?

members.quote: I'm ok approving this as-is, although I'm wondering if you looked at the possibility of using FUSE for this? Collection could still be opt-in (via env-var maybe), then they could be inspected live and measured over random chosen intervals instead.
members.note: APPROVED review body at the final head ef13273ba9; no inline comments. The PR's mechanism: CMake option TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS (default OFF), inline-variable counters in h/tron/kernels/page_share_counters.hpp, a static object's destructor prints to stderr at exit. Wade's alternative (FUSE + env var) later became PR #4596 TRON_ATTN_STATS, which publishes through the FUSE layer (memory files wade-fuse-question-pr4267.md, attn-stats-pr-implementation.md). needs_domain because knowing that FUSE is the team's preferred live-stats channel and that env-var opt-in is the convention comes from README.stats.md and team practice, though an agent with the repo can find README.stats.md. Design concern phrased as a question with alternatives and an explicit 'not a condition of approval', matching the skill's 'How Wade words a finding'.

members.concern: Part 2 of 2 (same comment id): most developers launch Perfetto through the wrapper script perfetto/tronperf, which forwards options to runtron, so a new runtron option is incomplete until the wrapper accepts and forwards it too.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a command-line option, environment variable or config knob to a binary that the repository also drives through a wrapper or launcher script (perfetto/tronperf, perfetto/wrapper, bin/*.sh, ci scripts).
detection.procedure: grep the new flag string across perfetto/, bin/, ci/, packaging/ and README files; list every launcher that forwards other options of the same binary (grep for an existing sibling flag such as --trace-gen in perfetto/tronperf) and check whether the new flag appears there too, including its usage/help text.
detection.question: Does every wrapper script that forwards sibling options to this binary also accept and forward the new option?

members.quote: The majority of runtron developers (if not all) use the perfetto/tronperf script to launch Perfetto against runtron. So that script needs an update to take this new parameter, and forward it to runtron (like it does other options today)
members.note: Verified: perfetto/tronperf at the final head 1c41d959 line 42 lists `--trace-passes SPEC` in its usage text, and the branch has a later commit 'Document --trace-passes in tronperf usage'; the file list shows perfetto/tronperf (+8 -1). Wade knows the operator workflow from team practice (which script people use), but the mechanism is checkable from the repository: a wrapper that forwards sibling flags. Wording: fact ('developers use the script'), 'So' consequence, concrete ask.

codex_bullets.bullet: Separate a computed work count from a measured time cost. Request comparable before-and-after measurements when the performance tradeoff matters. Label an unmeasured slowdown as a hypothesis and name the measurement that would decide it.
codex_bullets.reason: Three Wade comments (PRs 2898, 3733, 2713) ask for before/after trace data; the "Maybe it won't materialize" sentence in 4674512577 is Wade's own hedge after the paste. Claude skill only has the generic "name the check that would resolve" line. Note the tension with the Claude sentence "He does not comment on ... benchmark method".

codex_bullets.bullet: Define the unit being counted and the classification granularity. A forward containing prefill and decode work cannot establish decode-only behavior unless that limitation is explicit.
codex_bullets.reason: One strong comment (4596) and two weaker naming checks (3490, 2980). The second sentence is PR 4596 specific; adopt the first sentence only.

codex_bullets.bullet: Use stable worker or device identity for cumulative rows. Distinguish a pool thread from its temporary role. Verify exported names, debug strings, and documentation against the actual index.
codex_bullets.reason: Four comments (PRs 4596, 2980). The third sentence (exported names vs actual index) has two independent hits.

codex_bullets.bullet: Reuse existing configuration accessors and model parameters instead of copying environment reads or deriving a setting from a correlated dimension. Check that the normal wrapper or entry point exposes the feature.
codex_bullets.reason: Five quoted (PRs 3016, 2089, 2426, 2176, 3490); also 3029194687, 3036995239, 2915275194, 3866435051. One of the most frequent themes in the corpus. No Claude check.

codex_bullets.bullet: Do not turn an approved follow-up into a blocker.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 2766, 3490, 4267, 2980, 2176). Wade approves with follow-ups often (100 of 334 reviews approved, 0 changes requested); one sentence in the Claude skill would stop an agent from escalating these.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (severity words listed; no rule about follow-ups)

codex_bullets.bullet: For before-and-after runs, record revisions, build settings, model, workload, device, and environment. Inspect comparable trace regions. A memory-saving change can add repeated reconstruction work; distinguish the measured tradeoff from a workload-dependent regression.
codex_bullets.reason: Two Wade comments (PRs 2898, 3733) plus the 2906 paste. The third sentence is PR 2906 specific; adopt the first two.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (check 8 labels result revisions; nothing on trace comparison)
